metadata.title: Build Forgot Password API with Token Generation

story.iWant: request a password reset link via email
story.soThat: I can regain access to my account securely
story.tasks: - Create database migration for password_reset_tokens table - Implement POST /api/auth/forgot-password endpoint - Add JWT token generation with 1-hour expiration - Implement token invalidation logic (one active token per user) - Add email format validation - Implement rate limiting (3 requests per email per hour) - Add security measures to prevent email enumeration - Write unit tests for token generation - Write integration tests for forgot password flow

story-context.acceptanceCriteria:
### AC1: Password Reset Tokens Table Exists - Database includes password_reset_tokens table with columns: id, user_id (UNIQUE FK to users), token, expires_at, created_at - Index created on token column for fast lookups - ON DELETE CASCADE ensures orphaned tokens are removed when user is deleted
### AC2: Forgot Password Endpoint Accepts Email - POST /api/auth/forgot-password endpoint accepts JSON body with email field - Validates email format before processing - Normalizes email (trim, lowercase) for consistency
### AC3: Token Generation and Storage Logic - Generates JWT token with userId payload and 1-hour expiration - Uses existing JWT_SECRET from environment - Invalidates any existing reset tokens for the user before creating new one - Stores token in password_reset_tokens table with expiration timestamp
### AC4: Security - No Email Enumeration - Always returns 200 status with generic success message regardless of whether email exists - Message: "If an account exists with that email, a password reset link has been sent." - Prevents attackers from discovering valid email addresses
### AC5: Only One Active Token Per User - New password reset request deletes any existing active tokens for that user - Ensures only most recent token is valid - Prevents confusion and potential security issues from multiple active tokens

doc.title: Epic 11: Password Recovery & Account Security
doc.snippet: Enable users to securely reset forgotten passwords via email verification. Uses JWT tokens (1-hour expiration), stores reset tokens in database, sends emails via Nodemailer with Gmail SMTP. Secure reset links: /reset-password?token=JWT. One token per user (invalidate previous on new request).

doc.title: Smart Budget App Architecture
doc.snippet: Uses JWT (jsonwebtoken v9.0.2) for authentication with stateless, scalable approach. Passwords hashed with bcrypt. JWT_SECRET stored in environment configuration. Express.js backend with TypeScript, PostgreSQL database with pg driver.

doc.title: Smart Budget App Architecture
doc.snippet: PostgreSQL 14+ with node-pg-migrate for schema management. Migration pattern follows existing conventions in backend/migrations/ directory. Use pgm.createTable, pgm.createIndex patterns.

artifact.reason: Existing auth patterns show email validation, JWT token generation, bcrypt usage, and response formatting with sendSuccess/sendError utilities. Forgot password endpoint should follow same patterns.
Shows JWT verification pattern, error handling for expired/invalid tokens, and AuthRequest interface extension pattern.
Database pool export pattern for executing SQL queries. Use pool.query() for database operations.

Example migration showing pgm.createTable, pgm.createIndex patterns, data types (serial, varchar, timestamp), and constraints (notNull, unique, primaryKey). New password_reset_tokens migration should follow this pattern.
Standard response formatting utilities used throughout auth routes. Must use for consistent API responses.

story-context.constraints: - Must use existing JWT_SECRET from environment configuration - Follow migration naming convention: timestamp_description.js - Use node-pg-migrate API: pgm.createTable, pgm.createIndex - All endpoints must use sendSuccess/sendError response utilities - Email validation must use same pattern as registration endpoint - Database queries must use pool.query() from config/database.ts - All timestamps must use PostgreSQL TIMESTAMP type with NOW() default - Security: Always return success response (never reveal if email exists) - Rate limiting: Maximum 3 requests per email per hour - Token expiration: 1 hour (3600 seconds) - One active token per user: Delete existing tokens before creating new one - Token payload must include userId for validation - Log all password reset requests for security monitoring

tests.standards: Project uses integration-style tests with real database connections. Tests follow pattern: - Import service/route to test - Import database pool from config/database - beforeAll: Create test data - afterAll: Clean up test data and close pool connection - beforeEach: Reset state between tests - Use pool.query() for direct database operations in tests - Test files located in same directory as implementation (e.g., quota.service.test.ts) - Run with: npm test [filename]
tests.ideas:
- Test migration creates password_reset_tokens table with correct schema - Test migration creates index on token column - Test foreign key constraint references users table - Test ON DELETE CASCADE removes tokens when user deleted
- Test endpoint validates email format (reject invalid formats) - Test endpoint normalizes email (trim, lowercase) - Test endpoint returns 400 for missing email field - Test endpoint accepts valid email format
- Test JWT token generated with userId payload - Test token has 1-hour expiration - Test token uses JWT_SECRET from environment - Test token can be verified and decoded - Test old tokens are deleted before creating new one - Test token stored in database with correct expiration timestamp
- Test returns 200 success for non-existent email (no enumeration) - Test returns 200 success for existing email - Test both responses have identical structure and timing - Test generic success message never reveals email existence
- Test creating second token deletes first token - Test only one active token exists after multiple requests - Test most recent token is the valid one - Test old token becomes invalid after new request
- Test allows up to 3 requests per email per hour - Test 4th request within hour returns 429 error - Test rate limit resets after 1 hour - Test rate limiting is per-email (different emails not affected)
- Test complete flow: request reset → token created → stored in DB - Test token cleanup for deleted users (CASCADE) - Test concurrent requests for same email
